title: Steps to Diversify Sources of Seafood and Vegetable Items Ahead of Major Festivities to Mitigate Price Increases
what_it_is: Steps to Diversify Sources of Seafood and Vegetable Items Ahead of Major Festivities to Mitigate Price Increases

sections.label: Diversified vegetable and seafood imports
sections.summary: Top vegetable and seafood imports come from over 10 source countries, strengthening supply resilience, though festive demand raises prices.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Most of our top vegetable and seafood imports are well-diversified, with over 10 source countries, which include China, Vietnam, Indonesia, Australia, various European countries, the United States, United Kingdom, Canada and even Ecuador.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: This has helped to strengthen the resilience of our seafood and vegetable supplies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Nonetheless, prices of popular food items tend to rise ahead of festive periods because of a surge in demand.

sections.label: Food cost factors and government strategy
sections.summary: Food costs are influenced by imported prices, feed, energy, freight, labour, weather and supply disruptions, addressed by import diversification, local production and stockpiling.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: On the first one, he asked what are the factors that contribute to and influence the cost of food.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: There are a combination of factors and these include imported prices, animal feed, energy costs, freight costs, labour costs, seasonal weather patterns and possible supply chain disruptions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: I want to share with Mr Melvin Yong that the regional weather disruptions that are currently putting upside pressures on Singapore's imported food prices should fade as the monsoon season passes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: The general appreciation of the Singapore dollar against the currencies of many of our key import source countries will also continue to temper cost pressures.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: The Government has in place a multi-pronged strategy involving import diversification, local production "30 by 30" and also stockpiling to reduce the impact of unforeseen disruptions to our food supply.

sections.label: Food imported from 170 countries
sections.summary: Singapore imports its food from 170 countries worldwide.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Today, we import our food from 170 countries all over the world.
